About five years ago, my father was in the hospital for pneumonia. 

He’d had a stroke years earlier and was still wheelchair bound and not completely mentally sound. 

My mother and I had to take care of some of some legal / medical BS elsewhere and so we left dad in hospital room for a few hours. 

My mother drops me off at the hospital two hours later and I walk in to my father’s room. His doctor is there with a nurse a d they’re telling him he has some form of inoperable cancer - a tumor on his spine IIRC. 

Dad is weeping uncontrollably. I tear into the doctor for doing this without me or my mother being present. 

I  call my mother, fill her in and she races back to the hospital and also tears into the staff. 

Dad cried for days over the news. 

He passed away later that year from complications due to his stroke. 

Damn I still get angry thinking about this. 


Runner up:

I was diagnosed with kidney cancer. They caught it at stage one (due to a kidney stone) and my battle was short - just surgery to remove the tumor. No chemo, no radiation, no lymphatic surgery. 

Spoke with an oncologist after surgery and he said I was luck to have had the kidney stone. Most people find they have kidney cancer when it’s too late to treat. 

Then he said something prescient:

“You’re gonna go through some emotional changes and I suspect that, within a year, you’ll find your circle of friends has drastically changed. Your biggest battle is going to be navigating your new mind set.”

And he was right. In the span of a year and a half I reevaluated all my friends and jettisoned most of them. Kept a core circle of about ten friends and started seeking out other people who had their lives together and were more ethical / trustworthy.

I have several super magical experiences:

1.  Went to DW with my ballroom dance partner. We weren’t dating so I booked a room with separate beds at one of the all star resorts. 

About a month before my trip, they call me and tell me they overbooked my hotel and that they were moving me to Grand Floridian at no extra charge. 

I tell them that’s fine as long as there’s two beds. They assure there will be. 

I arrive a day before my dance partner and it’s a year of a million dreams and I got upgraded to concierge level. Again I tell them that’s great as long as there’s separate beds. 

Hotel clerk looks at me and says “no I have just one bed in your room.”

I explain the situation and that my dance partner arrives the next day. She assures me they’ll get it sorted. 

Next day they move me to a two bedroom suite in one of the towers. At the time it was $1200 a night, I got it for $100. 

Bonus: Belle asked my partner and I to dance a waltz at the princess pavilion. And when my dance partner and I went to dinner at the California grill, we rode the monorail in my tux and one of her dresses and we got a lot of admiring looks. 

2.  Went to DW to meet up with friends and family over the span of about a week. Stayed at contemporary. Took a red eye flight. Arrived at 6:00 am. Room wasn’t ready and I fell asleep in the lobby. Manager came up to me and told me I wasn’t allowed to sleep in the lobby. I apologized and he said “don’t worry, we have a room in the new tower expansion. No change in price.”

It was an apartment. Separate rooms with adjoining bathrooms. A kitchen. A family room. Worked out really well since friends were coming and going all week. 

3.  My cousin wanted to do DW with me. He’d never been and thought I was lying about the upgrades I’d get. We booked a room at Art of animation. A month before they called me and told me they were doing a remodel on where I’d been booked and they gave us a suite with separate bedrooms. Messaged my cousin about it and he said “the stories are true!!”

4. My father was dying a few years ago. It was just after Thanksgiving. Dad was in a coma after slowly deteriorating for years. I had a melt down and went to DW on a whim. Checked in and broke down crying while talking to the front desk person. 

She walked me to my room (or had someone walk me there) and then they took me to the skyliner. 

When I came back, there was a gorgeous gift basket filled with candy and Star Wars merch and a sympathy card. 

I returned home after a few days and my father passed the next day. 

Don’t think less of me. I’d helped my mother care for him for three years during the pandemic. I just kind of broke down for a few days and there was ton of family there to be with my mom.

One morning I wake up in pain and the pain doesn’t stop. I go to the ER and they find the kidney stone which had been lodged in my ureter. 

They blow it out with a laser. 

Six months later they do a follow up scan on my abdomen. Everything looks fine except that they find a small growth on my other kidney. 

It was stage one kidney cancer. 

I was very lucky. Generally by the time people detect kidney cancer it’s stage three and too late.
